name: Microsoft Dragon Copilot vs Freed
title: Microsoft Dragon Copilot vs Freed: Enterprise vs Solo AI Scribe Comparison
description: Compare Microsoft Dragon Copilot and Freed AI scribes. See differences in pricing, EHR integration, enterprise features, and target audiences.

summary.bottom_line: Microsoft Dragon Copilot is an enterprise platform combining ambient AI, dictation, and GPT-4 for large health systems with deep Epic integration. Freed is an affordable solo/small practice solution at $39-119/month. Choose Dragon Copilot for enterprise deployments with Microsoft/Epic ecosystems; choose Freed for accessible AI scribing without enterprise complexity.

key_differences.ehr_integration: Dragon Copilot (deep Epic/Cerner native) vs Freed (browser extension + select push)

sections.heading: Microsoft Dragon Copilot vs Freed: Overview
sections.content: Microsoft Dragon Copilot and Freed serve fundamentally different markets. Dragon Copilot is the healthcare industry's first unified voice AI assistant, combining ambient capture (DAX technology), clinical dictation (Dragon Medical One), and GPT-4 generation—designed for enterprise health systems with 100,000+ clinicians using it. Freed is a focused AI scribe for solo practitioners and small practices at accessible price points ($39-119/month). Dragon Copilot requires enterprise deployment; Freed can be used by any individual clinician today.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Freed has transparent public pricing: Starter ($39/mo), Core ($79/mo), Premier ($119/mo). Microsoft Dragon Copilot does not publish pricing—enterprise quotes are required, with industry estimates ranging $150-300+ per provider per month. Dragon Copilot bundles multiple technologies (ambient AI, dictation, GPT-4) that would cost more separately. For individual clinicians, Freed is the accessible option; for health systems, Dragon Copilot's bundled value may make sense at scale.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Dragon Copilot's key advantages are deep Epic/Cerner integration embedded directly in EHR workflows, voice dictation (Dragon Medical One), GPT-4 generation, nurse documentation support (2026), and clinical content partners (Elsevier, Wolters Kluwer). Freed's advantages are accessibility (free trial, transparent pricing), platform flexibility (works via browser extension with any EHR), and simplicity. Dragon Copilot is the more powerful enterprise solution; Freed is the more accessible individual solution.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: The choice is clear based on your organization type:

recommendations.when: You're part of a health system, your organization uses Epic or Cerner, you need nurse documentation support, or you want the most comprehensive AI clinical assistant with dictation
You're a solo practitioner or small practice, want transparent pricing you can sign up for today, prefer trying before buying (7-day free trial), or don't need enterprise-grade deployment
Your organization isn't ready for enterprise AI deployment—Freed lets individual clinicians start using AI documentation immediately without IT involvement

faqs.q: Can a solo doctor use Dragon Copilot?
faqs.a: Dragon Copilot is designed for enterprise health systems and requires organizational deployment. Solo doctors cannot easily sign up individually. Freed or Doximity Scribe are more accessible for individual clinicians.

faqs.q: Does Freed have dictation like Dragon Medical One?
faqs.a: Freed uses ambient AI to capture conversations but does not include traditional dictation like Dragon Medical One. If you need voice dictation for non-ambient documentation, Dragon Copilot or Dragon Medical One separately are better options.

Dragon Copilot has significantly deeper Epic integration, embedding directly into Epic workflows. Freed works with Epic via browser extension and copy-paste. For Epic-heavy organizations, Dragon Copilot's native integration is superior.

faqs.q: Is Dragon Copilot the same as Nuance DAX?
faqs.a: Dragon Copilot is the evolution of Nuance DAX, combining DAX ambient technology with Dragon Medical One dictation and GPT-4 generation into a unified platform. Microsoft acquired Nuance in 2022 and announced Dragon Copilot at HIMSS 2025.
